Theme

permanent adjective

also permanently, for good, lasting, long-lasting

classical

Cic. Brut. 105: quaestiōnēs perpetuae, standing courts (Lewis & Short: “a permanent tribunal”)
Ov. Tr. 3.10.14: perpetuamque facit

perpetuus, perpetua, perpetuum

adjective

permanent, lasting, unbroken

Lasting without a break, and so permanent: snow that never melts, a standing court. It also means continuous, whole: diem perpetuum, the whole day long (Ter. Ad.); ōrātiō perpetua, a continuous speech (Lewis & Short). Permanently, for good: in perpetuum (Cic. Cat. 1.30, Lewis & Short) or perpetuō.

Other words

  • perennis, perenne — lasting, never failing

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.107, of water that never fails (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. temporary: permanent

    From per annum: lasting the year round, and so of springs that never run dry, a hearth always alight, a work that endures (exēgī monumentum aere perennius, Hor. C. 3.30.1). Morgan–Owens gives it for permanent.

  • mānsūrus, mānsūra, mānsūrum — lasting, built to last

    adjective (future participle of <span lang="la">maneō</span>) · also used · classical · Verg. A. 3.86 (Lewis & Short, s.v. maneō: “lasting, permanent”); Tac. Ann. 14.20: mānsūram theātrī sēdem

    What is going to stay. Tacitus sets Pompey’s theatre, a seat built to last, against the stands put up for the occasion before it (see temporary).

Examples

  • nix jacet, et jactam nē sōl pluviaeque resolvant, indūrat Boreās perpetuamque facit

    snow lies, and once it has fallen, so that neither sun nor rain may melt it, the north wind hardens it and makes it permanentOv. Tr. 3.10.13–14

  • effinge aliquid et excūde, quod sit perpetuō tuum

    shape and hammer out something that will be yours for goodPlin. Ep. 1.3.4

  • rēs nōn parta labōre, sed relicta; nōn ingrātus ager, focus perennis

    means not won by toil but inherited; land that repays you; a hearth always alightMart. 10.47.3–4

  • Perenne conjugium animus, nōn corpus facit.

    A lasting marriage is made by the mind, not the body.Publil. Sent. P 54

See also always, long, temporary, constant.
